title: API keys
intro: API keys let you create links and check stats straight from your code, without opening the dashboard. Each key is an independent Bearer token: name it after where it will be used and revoke it when you no longer need it.

revokeDialog.title: Revoke this key?
revokeDialog.body: Integrations and scripts using this key will stop working immediately. This action cannot be undone.

empty.title: You don't have any API keys yet
empty.body: Create your first key in the form below to integrate Link Charts with your code: shorten links and track stats from any script, bot, or system.

create.heading: Create new key
create.nameHint: Just for you to identify where the key is used. Maximum of {{max}} characters.

validation.maxLength: The name can have at most {{max}} characters.

errors.limitReached: You reached the limit of {{max}} keys. Revoke an existing key to create another.
errors.rateLimited: Too many attempts in a row. Wait a minute and try again.
errors.generic: Could not create the key. Try again.

create.limitReachedNotice: You reached the limit of {{max}} API keys. Revoke an existing key to create another.

tokenDialog.title: Key created
tokenDialog.intro: This is your "{{name}}" key. Copy it and store it somewhere safe — for security, it will not be shown again.
tokenDialog.warning: Save it now: this is the only time the full key is shown. If you lose it, revoke this one and create another.

usage.heading: How to use the API
usage.intro: Every call carries the key in the Authorization header, as a Bearer token. With it you create short links and read click statistics from anywhere: an automation script, a bot, a CRM or spreadsheet integration.
usage.keepSecret: Treat the key like a password: don't commit it to Git or expose it in code that runs in the browser.
usage.rateLimit: Usage limit: 60 requests per minute per key. Responses include the X-RateLimit-Remaining header so you can pace yourself.

endpoints.heading: Available endpoints
endpoints.note: The API can't edit or delete links yet — use the dashboard for that.

createExample.title: Create a link
createExample.description: POST to /api/v1/links with the destination URL. The response includes the link id and the short URL.

subdomainExample.title: Create a link on a custom address
subdomainExample.description: Send subdomain with one of your address names — this example is pre-filled with yours ({{host}}). Omit the field for your default address; send null for the main domain.
subdomainExample.noAddress: You don't have a custom address yet. Claim yours and this example will show up here pre-filled with it.

statsExample.title: Read statistics
statsExample.description: GET /api/v1/links/{id}/stats returns the link's clicks — the id comes from the create response or from GET /api/v1/links.

errors.heading: Errors
errors.intro: Every error comes in the {"error": {"code", "message"}} envelope. The code is stable for handling in code; the message explains in plain text. The ones you may hit:

items.unauthenticated: 401 UNAUTHENTICATED — key missing, invalid or revoked.
items.validation: 422 VALIDATION_FAILED — some field is invalid; details.fields points to which.
items.invalidSubdomain: 422 INVALID_SUBDOMAIN — the subdomain sent is not an active address of your account.
items.notFound: 404 NOT_FOUND — the link does not exist or is not yours.
items.rateLimited: 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS — over 60 requests per minute; wait for Retry-After.

errors.safetyNote: Destination URLs flagged as dangerous (phishing/malware) are rejected with 422 — the same protection as the dashboard.
